area: dress-up, scripting, hazeljs: undo and redo of a script, on the usual keys
text: Undo and redo in the Scripting panel, on the usual keys. Ctrl+Z to undo and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo (⌘ on a Mac), for the script being edited, in text and in tiles alike. hazeljs has no undo of its own (it holds no editor: the page holds the text, its README says so since 11-03), so the game keeps each script's history: the texts it has had, one step per edit or per tiles edit message. A text box's own browser undo does not cover it: the page writes the tiles' edits into the boxes, which breaks the box's native history. Questions: whether Hazel's tiles frame (embed-editable) takes Ctrl+Z itself, and if so whose history wins; how a step is grouped (a word, a pause, a tiles edit). Also (Matthew, 11-03): console lines with timings, in ms: the cost of each edit, each undo and each redo.
source: Matthew, 2026-11-03, in chat, on hazeljs having no undo or redo: "in MUDU, it would be nice to bind them to the usual key combinations, for instance" Then: "in MUDU, i'd also like console messages that give timing information: * cost per edit * cost per undo * cost per redo -- in ms"

text: Bug in hazeljs 0.0.4 (#2719's library): key order matters for a labeled tuple with a list field. Hazel.run("fun (p : (x = Int, y = [Int])) -> p.x").value gives 5 for {x: 5, y: [1]} but {hazel: "...(Asc ..."} for {y: [1], x: 5}: stuck at the parameter's annotation. With only Int fields ({y: 3, x: 10}) the order does not matter. A JS object's keys have no order a JS developer thinks about, so the boundary should convert by the type's field order (or by label), not the object's. Where: the library's value conversion in (JS object to labeled tuple), and the cast it meets; check whether #2681 (no cast re-checked at run time) or ^ticket(681) (converting JS values directly) changes it. Until fixed: hazeljs-petri-example's node/petri.mjs builds its view in Net's field order and says why.
